advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the `dependency_hashes` comment (manifest.py:257-258) to reflect that the claim gate now re-hashes at the current gate ref, NOT the same pinned-SHA basis.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py:257-258: `# Hash through the shared boundary: during an attested review this is the pinned-SHA\n    # snapshot (the claim gate re-hashes the SAME basis); in local mode it is the checkout.`

The claim gate now calls `_hash_basis(repo_root, at_current_gate_ref=True)` (attest.py:675) which resolves to the CURRENT gate ref, not the signing pinned-SHA — so 'the claim gate re-hashes the SAME basis' is no longer true and is precisely the invariant the change intentionally broke.
advisory.finding: The `dependency_hashes` docstring comment still asserts the claim gate re-hashes the SAME basis as signing, but this change deliberately makes the two bases different (signing = review's pinned snapshot; claim gate = current gate ref). The stale comment describes the exact tautology that bug 72d9 removed.
advisory.suggested_fix: Reword the comment to: signing hashes at the review's pinned snapshot; the claim gate re-hashes the SAME PATHS but at the current gate ref (deliberately a different tree — see bug 72d9).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the `_gate_source_local` docstring in test_llm_optionality.py: rebar_repo now has a root commit (conftest.py:57), so justify the local pin by the actual reason (degradation seam, no signing) rather than an unresolvable HEAD.
evidence: tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_optionality.py:57-60: `The suite-wide default is ``attested``/``ref=HEAD`` (tests/conftest.py), but the shared ``rebar_repo`` fixture's repo has NO code-branch commit, so ``HEAD`` cannot resolve`
tests/interfaces/conftest.py:57: `_git("commit", "--allow-empty", "-q", "-m", "init", cwd=repo)` — this changeset gives rebar_repo a root commit, so HEAD now DOES resolve.
The degradation tests use `rebar_repo` (test_llm_optionality.py:113 `def test_library_operation_degrades_without_extra(op: str, rebar_repo: Path)`).
advisory.finding: The new `_gate_source_local` autouse fixture in test_llm_optionality.py justifies pinning `source=local` on the premise that 'the shared rebar_repo fixture's repo has NO code-branch commit, so HEAD cannot resolve' — but this same changeset adds a root commit to `rebar_repo` in tests/interfaces/conftest.py, so that premise is now false.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test signing a no-`verified_at_sha` (pre-S4b/local) attestation and running claim_gate_check under source=attested/ref=HEAD, asserting the legacy-tolerance verdict the docstring promises.
evidence: manifest.py:215-216 (docstring): "Legacy tolerance: an attestation with no ``verified_at_sha`` (pre-S4b) still verifies — its signed hashes are simply compared against the same current-gate-ref basis."
attest.py commit message / docs/adr/0002: "A pre-S4b attestation carries no ``verified-at-sha`` step; it still verifies, with its signed hashes compared against the same current-gate-ref basis."

test_ref_coherence.py:136-149 test_local_gate_config_uses_working_tree_basis_on_both_sides sets `monkeypatch.setenv("REBAR_GATE_SOURCE", "local")` — the only no-pin (`attested=False`) test, and it uses local config, so the working-tree-signed-hashes-vs-snapshot-basis case never runs.
ABSENCE: search for 'pre-S4b' / 'Legacy tolerance' across tests/ returns only the source=local comment; no test signs a no-pin attestation and then runs claim_gate_check under source=attested.
advisory.finding: The documented 'legacy tolerance' path — a pre-S4b attestation with no verified_at_sha, verified under the production attested gate config, comparing its working-tree-signed hashes against the current-gate-ref SNAPSHOT basis — has no test. The only no-pin/legacy test forces source=local (working tree on both sides); the attested-config legacy path (the production default) is untested.
scenarios: A plan reviewed/signed in a pre-S4b or local-signed manner (no verified_at_sha) is later evaluated by the claim gate under the production attested/current-gate-ref default: signed hashes came from the working tree, the gate re-hashes from a committed snapshot — a spurious stale-code (or missed drift) could result and no test would catch it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test in test_ref_coherence.py that signs with attested=False (no pin) but leaves REBAR_GATE_SOURCE=attested (suite default), then asserts claim_gate_check resolves the signed hashes against the current-gate-ref snapshot and yields the intended verdict (no spurious stale-code when dep content is unchanged at HEAD; stale-code only on a landed change).
